text: I first opened up my DMs- I had 'em closed, which is like traditionally the default on Twitter for a long time.
speaker: Ryan Hoover
context: Lenny asks Ryan about his practice of offering free advice to founders who DM him on Twitter. Ryan explains how he initially hesitated to open his direct messages because he expected to receive spam, but was surprised to find that wasn't the case. This led to him actively inviting founders to reach out for advice, which he then sometimes shares publicly (anonymized) as a form of micro-blogging.
text_ko: 제가 처음으로 다이렉트 메시지(DMs)를 열었어요 — 원래는 닫아놨었거든요. 트위터에서는 오랫동안 그게 기본값이었어요.
text_zh: 这是我第一次把私信(DMs)打开——之前一直关着，推特(Twitter)长期默认就是关着的。
text_es: La primera vez que abrí mis mensajes directos (DMs), los tenía cerrados —algo que durante mucho tiempo fue la opción por defecto en Twitter.
key_sentence: I had 'em closed, which is like traditionally the default on Twitter for a long time.
original_text: I first opened up my DMs- I had 'em closed, which is like traditionally the default on Twitter for a long time. 'Cause I was like, "Oh, if I open them up, I'll just get a bunch of spam and I don't need another inbox to- to call through." I opened it up quietly and, um, actually didn't get a lot of spam, uh, surprisingly.

vocabulary.definition: A default is a preset option or value that is automatically selected unless an alternative is specified by the user. In technology, it often refers to settings or configurations that are applied when no other choice is made.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, understanding defaults is crucial for user experience design, as they can significantly influence user behavior and decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'default' can imply a lack of active choice, which may carry a negative connotation in contexts where proactive decision-making is valued.

text: And maybe the biggest surprise was a lot of people are pretty vulnerable. These are strangers, founders who DM me saying, "Hey, I'm- we have three months runway left. We're running out of money. Here's a situation.
speaker: Ryan Hoover
context: Lenny asks what Ryan has learned from founders who DM him questions. Ryan explains that he was surprised by how vulnerable and authentic people are willing to be in private messages, sharing serious problems like running out of funding. He reflects on how founders typically have to project confidence publicly while dealing with significant challenges privately.
text_ko: 그리고 아마도 가장 놀랐던 건 많은 사람들이 꽤 취약하다는 점이었어요. 낯선 창업자들(founders)이 다이렉트 메시지(DM)로 저한테 "저희 런웨이(runway)가 세 달밖에 남지 않았어요. 자금이 거의 바닥나가고 있어요. 이런 상황이에요"라고 보내요.
text_zh: 也许最让我意外的是，很多人其实很脆弱。这些都是陌生人，都是创始人，会私信我 (DM) 说：“嗨，我……我们只剩三个月的跑道 (runway)，资金快见底了，情况是这样的：”
text_es: Y quizá lo que más me sorprendió fue que mucha gente estaba bastante vulnerable. Eran personas que no conocía, fundadores que me escribían por mensajes directos (DM) diciendo: "Oye, eh... nos quedan tres meses de margen de caja (runway). Se nos está acabando el dinero. Te explico la situación."
key_sentence: a lot of people are pretty vulnerable.
original_text: And maybe the biggest surprise was a lot of people are pretty vulnerable. These are strangers, founders who DM me saying, "Hey, I'm- we have three months runway left. We're running out of money. Here's a situation. What advice do you have?" Or just things that, you know, everyone has to wear this unfortunate mask is kind of the way I- what I used to describe it.

vocabulary.definition: Exposed to the possibility of being harmed or attacked, either physically or emotionally.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being vulnerable often refers to a company's financial or operational weaknesses that could be exploited by competitors or lead to failure.
vocabulary.nuance: While vulnerability can imply weakness, it can also indicate openness and honesty, especially in discussions about challenges faced by startups.

vocabulary.definition: The amount of time a company can operate before it runs out of cash, typically measured in months.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, runway is a critical metric for assessing a company's financial health and sustainability, influencing investment decisions and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: Runway is often discussed in terms of cash flow management and can indicate urgency for fundraising or cost-cutting measures.

vocabulary.definition: A set of circumstances in which one finds oneself; a state of affairs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'situation' often refers to the current state of a company or market, particularly when assessing challenges or opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can be neutral but may carry negative connotations depending on the context, especially if it refers to a crisis or problematic scenario.

text: I do spend time, ironically, like. challenging founders sometimes when they're thinking about raising or thinking about an idea to- to not raise. Um, people who are in tech, uh, especially, are certain bubbles of tech, that's the default.
speaker: Ryan Hoover
context: Lenny asks Ryan about his advice to founders considering whether to start a company, given how difficult startups are. Ryan explains that he often challenges founders who assume they need to raise venture capital immediately after having an idea. He points out that in certain tech circles, fundraising has become the default first step, even when it may not be necessary or appropriate.
text_ko: 아이러니하게도 저는 때때로 창업자들(founders)이 자금 조달(raising)을 고민하거나 오히려 투자를 받지 않는 쪽을 생각할 때, 그 판단을 도전적으로 물어보는 데 꽤 시간을 써요. 특히 테크(tech) 업계에 있는 사람들은 특정 테크 버블(bubbles of tech)에 갇혀 있는 게 기본값(default)인 경우가 많아요.
text_zh: 说来有点讽刺，我有时会花时间去反问创始人 (founders)：当他们在考虑要不要融资 (raising) 或者在琢磨一个点子时，我会劝他们别急着去融资。特别是在科技圈 (tech) 的某些小圈子里，去融资几乎是默认的做法。
text_es: A veces, irónicamente, suelo retar a los fundadores: cuando están pensando en levantar fondos (raising) o cuando surge una idea, les planteo que quizá no deberían levantar fondos. La gente que está en tecnología, sobre todo en ciertas burbujas del sector, da por hecho que esa es la opción por defecto.
key_sentence: In certain bubbles of tech, that's the default to raise money immediately.
original_text: I do spend time, ironically, like. challenging founders sometimes when they're thinking about raising or thinking about an idea to- to not raise. Um, people who are in tech, uh, especially, are certain bubbles of tech, that's the default. It's like, "The first thing I do, I have an idea, now let's go raise money."

vocabulary.definition: Default refers to a pre-set condition or standard that is automatically applied unless an alternative is specified.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, default settings in software applications can significantly influence user behavior and decision-making processes.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can also imply a lack of action or choice, suggesting complacency or an unexamined status quo.

vocabulary.definition: Founders are individuals who establish or create a company or organization, often taking on significant risk and responsibility.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, founders are crucial as they drive the vision, culture, and initial growth of their ventures, often seeking investment to scale their ideas.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'founder' carries a sense of innovation and leadership but can also imply a level of inexperience in navigating business challenges.

text: I think it's super important that founders see a line of sight to work on this for ... I think my rule of thumb is a decade, just do you see yourself working on this for a decade?
speaker: Ryan Hoover
context: Ryan continues discussing his advice for founders considering starting a company. He explains his framework for evaluating startup commitment - founders should be able to envision working on their idea for a decade. While acknowledging that most startups fail before reaching that timeframe, he believes this long-term perspective serves as an important litmus test for genuine passion and commitment to the problem they're trying to solve.
text_ko: 창업자가 앞으로 이 일을 계속해나갈 수 있겠다는 그림을 그려볼 수 있는지가 정말 중요해요. 제 경험칙은 대략 10년이에요. 스스로 이걸 10년 동안 해나갈 수 있을 것 같으세요?
text_zh: 我觉得特别重要的一点是，创始人得能看出这件事有长期可走的路。我的经验是把时间拉到十年：你能想象自己为这件事坚持十年吗？
text_es: Creo que es muy importante que los fundadores puedan ver una vía clara para trabajar en esto. Mi regla general es una década; es decir, ¿se ven trabajando en esto durante diez años?
key_sentence: Founders should see a line of sight to work on this for a decade.
original_text: I think it's super important that founders see a line of sight to work on this for ... I think my rule of thumb is a decade, just do you see yourself working on this for a decade? And maybe it's not a decade that you actually work on it. It probably won't, it either, it'll probably fail before then as most startups do, but I think it's a good litmus test for yourself.

vocabulary.definition: A general principle or guideline based on practical experience rather than a strict rule.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a rule of thumb can help entrepreneurs make quick decisions based on past experiences or common practices, especially in uncertain situations.
vocabulary.nuance: While useful, a rule of thumb should not replace thorough analysis or data-driven decision-making.

text: I don't know how to articulate that- that feeling, but that flutter in your stomach that you wake up with in the morning of just anxiety and stress and- and worry.
speaker: Ryan Hoover
context: Ryan is describing the emotional toll of being a founder during difficult periods at Product Hunt. He's explaining to Lenny the physical manifestation of startup stress - the stomach flutter of anxiety upon waking. He emphasizes how being in a leadership position compounds this difficulty because founders must project confidence externally while dealing with internal anxiety, creating additional pressure beyond the underlying business challenges.
text_ko: 그 느낌을 어떻게 표현해야 할지 모르겠어요. 아침에 일어나자마자 속이 울렁거리고 불안하고 스트레스 받고 걱정으로 가득한 그런 기분이에요.
text_zh: 我说不上来那种感觉，就是早上醒来心里七上八下、肚子里翻腾，满是焦虑、压力和担忧。
text_es: No sé cómo explicarlo: esa sensación, ese nudo en el estómago con el que te despiertas por la mañana, simplemente de ansiedad, estrés y preocupación.
key_sentence: that flutter in your stomach that you wake up with in the morning of just anxiety and stress and- and worry.
original_text: I don't know how to articulate that- that feeling, but that flutter in your stomach that you wake up with in the morning of just anxiety and stress and- and worry. Um, being a CEO or founder makes it slightly harder, uh, in some ways, because you still have to put on this mask.

vocabulary.definition: To express an idea or feeling fluently and coherently. It involves the ability to convey thoughts clearly and effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, being articulate is crucial for effective communication during presentations, meetings, and negotiations, as it helps convey complex ideas succinctly.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'articulate' generally has a positive connotation, it may imply that someone is overly verbose if used inappropriately.

vocabulary.definition: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome. It can manifest physically and mentally.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, anxiety can affect employee performance and decision-making, often leading to decreased productivity and morale.
vocabulary.nuance: Anxiety can be a normal response to stress, but excessive anxiety may indicate deeper issues that require attention.

vocabulary.definition: A state of mental or emotional strain resulting from challenging or adverse circumstances. It can impact both physical and psychological well-being.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business environments, stress is often linked to tight deadlines, high expectations, and workload, which can lead to burnout if not managed effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While stress can sometimes motivate individuals to perform better, chronic stress is detrimental and should be addressed proactively.

text: The biggest surprise has probably been ... There are cases when I didn't think the company would make it.
speaker: Ryan Hoover
context: Lenny asks Ryan what has surprised him most about angel investing. Ryan explains that his biggest surprise has been seeing companies he had mentally written off as failures eventually succeed through pivots or unexpected breakthroughs. This taught him never to count portfolio companies out until they're definitively done, highlighting the unpredictable nature of startup journeys and the importance of backing resilient founders.
text_ko: 가장 놀라웠던 건 아마도… 회사가 버티지 못할 거라고 생각했던 순간들이 있었다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 最大的惊讶大概是……有好几次我都觉得公司撑不下去了。
text_es: Probablemente lo que más me ha sorprendido... Ha habido momentos en los que no creí que la empresa iba a salir adelante.
key_sentence: There are cases when I didn't think the company would make it.
original_text: The biggest surprise has probably been ... There are cases when I didn't think the company would make it. I- uh, either the product wasn't working, and you know, many months had passed, and it was very clear that they're- they- well, to me, I thought it was clear that, okay, that this probably isn't gonna work out. In my head I kinda wrote it off.

vocabulary.definition: An unexpected event or occurrence that causes astonishment or shock.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a surprise can refer to unforeseen outcomes in market trends, financial results, or project developments that can significantly impact strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'surprise' can have a positive connotation, such as a pleasant surprise in sales growth, it can also imply negative outcomes, making it essential to clarify the context.
